t.6.10.1: To Vibhīṣaṇa, who had spoken well-reasoned and beneficial words, Rāvaṇa, driven on by Time, spoke harsh words.
t.6.10.2: One may live together with a rival or with an enraged venomous serpent, but one should never dwell with one who, while professing friendship, serves the enemy.
t.6.10.3: I know the nature of kinsmen in all the worlds, O Rākṣasa: these kinsmen always rejoice in the misfortunes of their kinsmen.
t.6.10.4: O Rākṣasa, kinsmen indeed despise one who is foremost, accomplished, learned and righteous in conduct, and they humiliate the valiant.
t.6.10.5: Kinsmen always rejoice at one another's misfortunes and turn murderous in times of calamity; with their true hearts concealed, they are dreadful and a source of danger.
t.6.10.6: Verses are heard, sung once by elephants in a lotus grove on seeing men with nooses in their hands; listen to them as I recite them.
t.6.10.7: Neither fire nor other weapons nor nooses bring fear to us; but terrible kinsmen, driven by their own self-interest, are what bring fear to us.
t.6.10.8: These will tell them the means for the capture; there is no doubt about this. Fear from one's kinsmen is more grievous than every other fear, and this is known to us.
t.6.10.9: In cows is found abundance, in a brāhmaṇa self-restraint, in women fickleness, and from a kinsman comes danger.
t.6.10.10: Therefore, gentle one, this is not welcome: that I am honored by the world, have come into sovereignty, and stand upon the heads of my enemies.
t.6.10.12: Thus addressed with harsh words, Vibhīṣaṇa, who spoke what was just, sprang up into the air, mace in hand, together with four rākṣasas.
t.6.10.11: Had anyone else spoken such words as these, O night-ranger, he would not live past this very moment. But fie on you, you disgrace to our family!
t.6.10.13: Then the glorious Vibhīṣaṇa, filled with anger and standing in the sky, spoke these words to his brother, the lord of the Rākṣasas.
t.6.10.14: You are my brother, O king, so say to me whatever you wish; but this harsh and untrue speech of yours I will not tolerate.
t.6.10.15: O Daśānana, those of undisciplined mind who have come under the sway of Time do not accept well-reasoned words spoken by one who wishes them well.
t.6.10.16: O king, men who always speak pleasing words are easy to find; but one who speaks what is unpleasant yet wholesome, and one who listens to it, are hard to find.
t.6.10.18: I do not wish to see you slain by Rāma with his sharp, gold-adorned arrows, which resemble blazing fire.
t.6.10.17: I ought not to stand by and neglect one who is bound by the noose of Time, the carrier-off of all beings, and who is perishing, just as one would not neglect a dwelling that is ablaze.
t.6.10.19: Even those who are heroic, mighty, and skilled in weapons, when seized by Time, sink down on the field of battle like dams made of sand.
t.6.10.21: O night-ranger, though I, who wish you well, try to hold you back, my words do not please you. For men whose time has come and whose life is spent do not accept the wholesome counsel spoken by their friends.
t.6.10.20: Protect yourself in every way, and this city too along with its rākṣasas. May it go well with you; I shall depart. Be happy without me.
